Maximum absolute difference 0.000e+00 on all 11 real gpt2 adjacent-layer pairs (N=12895, D=768; e.g. pair 0-1 both 0.983369004969, pair 10-11 both 0.882819004431) and 0.000e+00 over 20 random (1000,10) pairs. Analytic anchors hold: an exact Y = X A gives exactly 1.0; the score is invariant to rescaling (0.995579937940 identical at x1e-14 and x1e+14), to right-rotation of X or Y, and to an exact zero-padding isometry D 20 -> 128 (0.9955799379398909 both, and the rank-aware companion agrees). comparable_reason: The score is an OLS goodness-of-fit with D free parameters per output coordinate on N points, so it is deflated by the chance-fit factor and moves with BOTH width and token count on synthetic data with the generative residual HELD FIXED at 0.10. At N=1024, 1-sim falls monotonically 0.009757491 (D=16) -> 0.007433290 (D=256), Pearson r = -0.9999953, Spearman rho = -1.000000. At D=64, 1-sim rises 0.004896243 (N=128) -> 0.009580964 (N=2048), rho = +1.000000, i.e. +95.7%. On the real gpt2 (5,6) pair the same effect appears end to end: 0.999974714 at N=800 -> 0.996167890 at N=12895. Because N is whatever the tokenizer emits from a fixed corpus, tokenizer efficiency enters the comparison as well. The shipped `_meta_d_over_n_tokens` = 0.0596 documents the regime but does not correct it.

This is the algebra of a D-parameter least-squares fit, not a property of the layer map, so a wider model scores as 'more linear' for identical geometry.
